News.title: Mystery remains around Jordan Wright’s tragic death after Towie star, 33, found lifeless in Thai drainage ditch
News.content:
MYSTERY remains around Jordan Wright’s death one month after the Towie star’s body was found in a Thai ditch.

The 33-year-old from Basildon, Essex, was found face down in a drainage canal on the island of Phuket on March 14.





An inquest into Wright’s death opened today at Chelmsford Coroner’s Court.

But his cause of death is yet to be made public with vital information still expected from a toxicology report from Thailand.

The case was adjourned until September 14.



Now his family must endure further excruciating months without answers as questions still swirl around his death and key details remain a mystery.

The reality TV star had only moved to the paradise country weeks earlier in search of a fresh start.

Wright was reportedly discovered by a Burmese worker in a ditch near Bang Tao Beach.

Local cops rushed to the scene and confirmed there were no signs of physical assault or struggle.



His iPhone 17 was found on the bank nearby. A key card discovered in his pocket helped officers identify him.

Cops also confirmed a search of his hotel room showed no signs of forced entry or anything suspicious.

Chilling CCTV footage appeared to show Wright pacing erratically outside a hotel shortly before his death.

In the grainy night-time video, Wright suddenly grabs onto a parked white pickup truck to steady himself as he stumbles around a corner.

He appears disoriented, almost panicked, before pushing on.



CCTV then shows him pacing back and forth before suddenly bolting out of the complex again and vanishing into the darkness beyond the hotel perimeter.

Wright is believed to have sprinted across rough, uneven fields surrounding the hotel before leaping down a 10ft creek, splashing through a shallow stream and scrambling towards a nearby construction site.

Separate footage, obtained by The Sun, captured the ITV personality getting into a furious row with a mystery stranger while standing at the ditch just 12 minutes later.

In the CCTV clip, a family of three staying at a neighbouring hotel can be seen walking down a path as Wright is heard yelling angrily.

Police said he had been staying alone at Hotel COCO Phuket Bangtao and was due to check out the day before he was found.



Police believe he was arguing over the phone.

It has not been confirmed what exactly Wright was shouting, but at points he appears to say: “Before they come back, let’s get them back in the head and have a f**king shootout.”

Police Lieutenant Colonel Chanasin Prateep Na Thalang said that a “foreign family of three staying at The Title Hotel” saw Wright walking alone.



They said he was by the “drainage canal, shouting loudly as if he was in a frenzied state”.

The family then “heard the sound of someone wading in the water”, Thalang said.

He added: “Then at around midnight, the noise went quiet.”

Officers investigating the case say Wright is believed to have drowned in the stagnant water, but that his exact time of death is not known.

As well as probing his apparent phonecall, cops are also investigating anyone who the former reality star had met earlier in the evening.



Immigration paperwork shows Wright arrived in Thailand on December 3, 2025, on a Digital Nomad visa, often used by backpackers for moving across Asia.

Before finding fame, Jordan had worked as a firefighter.

He later admitted he felt “hugely unfulfilled” by TV life and eventually returned to the job.

He rose to fame on Ex On The Beach in 2017 before joining The Only Way Is Essex in 2018.

Jordan also dated reality star Vicky Pattison and was known for his explosive storyline with Courtney Green and Myles Barnett.



Tributes poured in for the late star following his sudden death.

Fellow Towie star Chloe Brockett wrote: “Rest in peace Jordan” and heart emoji.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another wrote: “Oh Jord, gone way too soon. Rest in peace darling.”

A third said: “Oh Jord! This is heartbreaking to hear. You’ll be truly missed.”

News.title: Tenerife cops arrest man who sexually assaulted Brit tourist in ‘lion killer’ chokehold – hours before mugging UK couple
News.content:
SICK RAMPAGE Tenerife cops arrest man who sexually assaulted Brit tourist in ‘lion killer’ chokehold – hours before mugging UK couple

A MAN who allegedly sexually assaulted a British tourist and beat up a pensioner couple from the UK on the same day has been arrested.

Tenerife police detained the 22-year-old, who is accused of using a martial arts “lion killer” chokehold to overpower the woman after pretending to help her look for her lost mobile phone.



Cops said the man sexually assaulted the Brit tourist while she was “semi-conscious” and only did not rape her after she promised not to report him.



The alleged attack took place on the Playa de las Americas beach, in the south of Tenerife.

But the man didn’t stop there.

Police said after the sexual assault, the same suspect went on to violently mug an elderly couple from the UK.

An 89-year-old British man and his 79-year-old wife were hospitalised after the mugging.

The suspect allegedly lashed out in anger when the man’s wife threw her husband’s watch into a bush during the struggle.

Revealing details of the latest arrest, a spokesman for Spain’s National Police said: “A young woman who had lost her mobile phone started looking for it in the vicinity with a man who had offered to help her.

“Taking advantage of the fact they were in a secluded and lonely place, the individual attacked her by surprise, using a technique known as a ‘lion killer chokehold which left her semi-conscious, and then sexually assaulting her.”

He said that the alleged attacker kicked and punched the pensioners during the mugging, adding: “The mugger tried to steal the man’s watch, and a tussle occurred between both, which ended with the watch on the floor.



“At this moment the man’s wife picked it up and threw it into an area of bushes to avoid it being taken.

“This provoked a violent reaction by the attacker who assaulted both victims with his fists and his feet, managing finally to take a bag full of their shopping that they were carrying.”

News.title: Woman, 19, mauled to death by family dog at home suffered ‘serious traumatic neck injuries’, inquest told
News.content:
A YOUNG woman mauled to death at home by a family dog suffered serious neck injuries, an inquest heard today.

Jamie-Lea Biscoe, 19, was discovered by her dad Jack Biscoe at home in Uttlesford, Essex, on April 10.





Tragically, she could not be saved and was declared dead at the scene shortly after.

An inquest heard today how Jamie-Lea sustained “serious traumatic injuries to her neck”, which were suspected to have been “caused by one of the family dogs”.

A post-mortem gave a provisional cause of death as “neck injuries pending investigation of histology and toxicology”.



Lincoln Brookes, Senior Coroner for Essex, described the horror as a “truly tragic loss of life”.

He adjourned the inquest until a later date pending a criminal investigation.

Jack told The Sun how he found Jamie-Lea slumped over on the floor with a bite wound to her neck.

Part of his ear was bitten off by the dog and he was left with puncture wounds to his arm after he was also attacked.



He said he pleaded with police, who seized the female blue-merle Lurcher-cross Shy to put her to sleep immediately.

The dad-of-one, 37, added: “I just said to them ‘please just put her down’.

“I don’t want to see her ever again… I just don’t think that dog should live anymore.”

Police previously confirmed that tests are underway to formally establish Shy’s breed.

They are also understood to be conducting forensic examinations to prove she carried out the fatal attack.



The family’s other dogs Bella and Mouse – Shy’s 18-month-old pups – are not thought to have been involved in the attack which killed Jamie-Lea.

But horse trainer Jack is also calling for them to be destroyed as he believes they have “seen too much”.

The dad continued: “My daughter was not killed by an XL Bully, she was killed by a genuine family dog.

“I thought I could trust that dog with my life and it took my daughter’s life. She was my daughter’s best friend and she still killed her.

“I lost my entire life on Friday when my daughter was murdered by another member of my family.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Witnessing the horror and destruction it has caused me, it’s not worth it. Treat them as dogs, give them their beds, be careful.”

Jack was arrested on suspicion of being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control and causing injury resulting in death but was released on bail.

News.title: Brit, 70, plunged two floors into koi pond at Lanzarote hotel after ‘losing his balance’ while looking down at water
News.content:
POND HORROR Brit, 70, plunged two floors into koi pond at Lanzarote hotel after ‘losing his balance’ while looking down at water

A BRITISH tourist plunged from the second floor of a five-star Lanzarote hotel into a shallow pond below after losing his balance.

The 70-year-old man landed in the knee-high pond filled with different types of exotic fish late on Saturday night.





One source said: “It appears he was on the second floor with his wife and peered down to take a look at the fish pond below before losing his balance and falling.”

The pond, thought to be two floors below street level by a hotel restaurant, was only about 15 inches deep.

By the time firefighters arrived, medical staff had already fitted the elderly tourist with a neck brace.

Emergency crews fished him out of the pond before rushing him into a waiting ambulance.

The victim was then taken to Molina Orosa Hospital in island capital Arrecife.

His current condition remains unknown.

Hotel staff at the five-star H10 Rubicon Horizons Collection in Playa Blanca refused to comment on the situation due to “client confidentiality”.

The seafront adults-only establishment describes itself online as an iconic resort with an interior inspired by the island landscape.



Local police and Civil Guard officers were also mobilised in the immediate aftermath of the incident, with one saying the situation is being treated as “an accident”.

It comes after a man died at Lanzarote Airport in February, just minutes after arriving on a plane from the UK.

The victim is said to have collapsed in the queue for passport control less than half an hour after disembarking his Jet2 flight.

The aircraft is understood to have touched down at 2.25pm with the alarm raised just 22 minutes later at 2.48pm.

Emergency services rushed to the distressing scene in Terminal One, but were unable to save him.



The man was pronounced dead shortly before 3pm local time.

In the aftermath, Civil Guard sources confirmed the incident was not being treated as suspicious.

Local reports instead pointed to a suspected heart attack.

Sources ruled out any link between the tragedy and the long queues British holidaymakers report when passing through passport control.

News.title: Horror moment Nigerian migrant kills cat and tries to COOK it at a children’s playground in broad daylight
News.content:
‘BARBARIC’ ATTACK Horror moment Nigerian migrant kills cat and tries to COOK it at a children’s playground in broad daylight

THIS is the moment a man “tries to cook a cat he killed in broad daylight” at a children’s playground.

Cops raced to the park after receiving multiple horrified phone calls about a man, identified as a Nigerian migrant, who said he was hungry.





In photos from the scene, the man can be seen crouching above a makeshift grill where he allegedly attempted to roast the body of a grey cat.

A colourful children’s slide can be seen just feet away from where the man is poking the fire with a stick.

The man was caught by locals conducting the twisted cook out at Crociata Park, in Italy‘s northeast town of Sarzana on April 15.

Cops said the man was stood far away from the animal and the fire was out when they arrived.



They arrested him on suspicion of animal cruelty but it’s understood his arrest was temporary and no charges were filed against him, Cittadella Spezia reports.

Police were unable to determine whether the animal was killed by the man or was already dead.

Local animal protection groups have expressed their outrage and called for “rigorous prosecution”.

Piera Rosati, president of LNDC Animal Protection said while it was important to understand that the lives of homeless people can be extremely difficult, it cannot justified “serious acts of violence against animals”.



“There are facilities and services capable of guaranteeing a hot meal to those in need,” she said.

“Killing an animal in a cruel manner and in a public place is never acceptable and must be prosecuted with the utmost severity.”

Some Italian politicians have spoke out against the act.

Italy’s Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini called the act “heinous” that must not go unpunished.”

Security Councillor Stefano Torri also called the act “atrocious” with no place in “civilised society”.



He added that the park had been long-abandoned and needed investment to “bring positive community, order, light and legality to this area.”

Right-wing Italian MP Michela Vittoria Brambilla called for the act “barbaric”.

“Anyone who tramples on the life of an animal tramples on the values ​​of our community,” she said.

The Sun has contacted Sarzana Police for comment.

News.title: Terrorist who was jailed for planning to bomb London Stock Exchange was allowed to stay in UK on human rights grounds
News.content:
TERROR FARCE Terrorist who was jailed for planning to bomb London Stock Exchange was allowed to stay in UK on human rights grounds

A TERRORIST who was jailed for planning to bomb the London Stock Exchange was allowed to stay in the UK on human rights grounds.

Shah Rahman was one of four al-Qaeda-inspired extremists locked up in 2012 over the sick plot to bomb the capital.





Now, a judgment in an immigration case has revealed the Bangladeshi national has been permitted to stay in the UK – even though his asylum claim failed.

Rahman applied for asylum in 2017, the same year he was first released on licence.

His claim was initially rejected under the Refugee Convention, which allows officials to deny status to those guilty of terrorist acts or serious crimes.

However, he was still granted restricted leave to remain.

The judgment states he could not be removed to Bangladesh because it would breach his rights under Article 3 of the Human Rights Convention.

And the rule provides an absolute right of protection from torture or degrading treatment.

The details emerged following a legal battle involving Rahman”s wife, Parveen Purbhoo, who can be named for the first time after restrictions were lifted.

Purbhoo, a Mauritian citizen, married Rahman in an Islamic ceremony in London in June 2019.



After this, she applied for entry clearance to the UK, which was initially denied but granted after she applied a second time.

But she has now been permanently excluded from Britain after Isis-related imagery was discovered on her phone at Heathrow.

The court heard Purbhoo was stopped by immigration officers in August 2021.

Her phone contained Jihadist propaganda and videos of soldiers.

Despite the discovery, she was allowed to enter the UK and lived with Rahman until his arrest in 2022.



A police report presented to the court found: “She appeared very blasé about having them on her mobile.

“She could not remember where or how they got there.

“She admitted that she wanted to learn more about it and what it was and about the atrocities.”

Rahman was recalled to prison in February 2022 and convicted for failing to notify probation of a mobile phone, email address, and bank account.

The judgment said: “Mr Rahman accepted before the parole board that he would use the illicit mobile phone to contact the applicant.



“In his witness statement in these proceedings, he accepts that he used the phone to have private video calls with her.”

A forensic psychology report by the parole board also found Purbhoo was “complicit in the breaches for which Mr Rahman was convicted”.

In 2023, then-Home Secretary Suella Braverman permanently excluded Purbhoo from the UK.

In a verdict published on Monday, Purbhoo was denied the right to appeal against her exclusion.

Mrs Justice Farbey, Mark Ockelton and Roger Golland found: “The applicant was complicit in Mr Rahman’s unlawful breach of notification requirements; and she has not provided either the police or SIAC with an explanation of how Islamist material came to be on her phone.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Her willingness to place her own interests over and above legal or administrative processes is troubling and risky.”

SIAC’s judgment found that she had been “reasonably assessed as a national security risk” and the decision to exclude her had been proportionate.

News.title: Emmerdale and Happy Valley star found dead at home aged 41 – hours after being quizzed by cops
News.content:
ACTOR TRAGEDY Emmerdale and Happy Valley star found dead at home aged 41 – hours after being quizzed by cops

AN ACTOR who starred in Emmerdale and Happy Valley took his own life just hours after he was arrested and quizzed by police.

Frazer Hammill was found dead at his home aged 41 on December 30 last year, after leaving a note on his neighbour’s door with the keys to his house, an inquest heard.



The note instructed the neighbour to not enter but call the cops as he had taken his own life.



Frazer appeared as a prison guard in Emmerdale and as a police officer in the hit BBC drama Happy Valley.

The “talented and kind-hearted” actor had been arrested by Lancashire Police a day earlier, reports YorkshireLive.

When he left the station he “appeared to be in good spirits” custody officers told Doncaster Coroner’s Court.

The police said they had no concerns over his safety or mental well-being, reports Yorkshire Live.



The area coroner, Louise Slater, concluded the actor’s medical cause of death was “1a hanging”.

She added: “Frazer Hammill passed away at his home on December 30. He was a single man, an actor, and very close to his family members.”

When police and paramedics arrived at Frazer’s flat just after 2pm he could not be resuscitated and his time of death was recorded at 2.13pm she continued.

The coroner said Frazer had left further notes for his family and friends following his arrest.



“Therefore, I am satisfied that this was a deliberate act and Frazer had put thought, planning and intention into his actions,” she concluded and offered her condolences to his loved ones.

The inquest heard a statement from Frazer’s sister Caroline Hammill who said his death was a “complete shock” to the family.

No one was aware of the actor’s struggles with mental health or that he was “feeling low enough to end his life”.

Caroline said her brother was “happy in life” and “loved his family and nieces and nephews”.

The John Godber Company issued a tribute for the star and said it is “impossible to put into words how much he will be missed by all of us who had the absolute joy of working with him”.



It added: “Frazer had a huge loving heart and enormous talent. We are all heartbroken.”

Fellow actor, Lamin Touray who performed with Frazer posted on social media: “You were one of the most talented, funny, kind-hearted, loyal, caring, wise people I’ve ever met; you taught me so much.”

He continued: “One of the most talented actors who became more than just a friend and colleague, you became family.

“You met my daughter just a few weeks ago. You came to watch the boxing at my house. All my family loved you and always spoke so highly of you!

“Me and you spoke about our big plans for 2026. We set goals and aims. You were in such a good place emotionally, career-wise, FLYING, but it wasn’t enough to keep you with us.”



Theatre Royal Wakefield also paid tribute on social media to Frazer.

It added: “We are saddened to hear the news of Frazer Hammill’s passing.

Frazer was not only a talented actor who graced our stage but a wonderful collaborator and friend to so many of us over the years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“His warmth, professionalism and passion for his craft left a lasting impression on everyone he worked with.

“Our thoughts are with his family, friends, and all who knew him. He will be greatly missed.”

News.title: Sick school shooting fanatic named after horror attack on tourists at Mexican pyramids on Columbine massacre anniversary
News.content:
A GUNMAN who opened fire at a world-famous landmark and killed one tourist and injured two children was a school shooter fanatic.

Julio César Jasso Ramírez, 27, has been named as the suspected killer who shot dead a Canadian woman and injured 13 others yesterday at the Teotihuacán Pyramids in Mexico.





Yesterday’s horrifying attack occurred on the 27th anniversary of the infamous massacre, when 13 students and one teacher were killed in a shooting and attempted bombing at Columbine High School in Colorado.

Witnesses said Jasso held holidaymakers hostage and fired more than 20 shots.

After raining bullets on terrified tourists, the killer turned the weapon on himself.

A six-year-old Colombian boy and a 13-year-old Brazilian girl were hospitalised following the attack, alongside 11 other injured holidaymakers.

It emerged overnight that the sick shooter was a Nazi sympathiser who idolised the two students behind the 1999 Columbine High School massacre.

Mexican TV station Telediario reported a picture frame was found near Jasso’s body containing an AI-generated image where he appeared next to Harris and Klebold, who also killed themselves after committing their April 20 1999 horror massacre.

Authorities also found photos of Jasso on social media making Nazi salutes, it said.



Prosecutors investigating the shooting, who identified Jasso by a voter ID card he was carrying, are currently working on the theory that he acted alone.

It was also claimed the gunman was wearing a T-shirt emblazoned with a logo reading “Disconnect & Self-Destruct”.

This was linked by the Mexican media to a true crime community that includes a dangerous subculture known as “Columbiners” who obsess over school shooters Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold.

Shocking footage from the site shows an armed man shooting from the top of The Pyramid of the Moon.

One woman was heard screaming in the background for someone to call the police and tourists could also be seen hiding at the base of the pyramid.



The shaky handheld footage also captured people attempting to flee the stray bullets.

Laura Torres, a Mexican tourist who witnessed the attacks, told N+ that the shooter held several hostages.

She said: “I saw the guy who was shooting up on the pyramid… he had people as hostages, after a short time I saw him let one person down, a girl.



“For a moment I thought he was going to shoot her in the back, but no, thank God he let her go.

“After a short while he let another guy down, the same, but the hostages were still there.”

Laura said she heard more than 20 gunshots, and saw a tourist being shot.

She added: “She was lying about halfway up the pyramid… This shouldn’t have happened.”

The 32-year-old Canadian woman killed has not been named.



A total of 13 others, including a six-year-old boy and a 13-year-old Brazilian girl, were taken to hospital for their injuries.

Both of the children had gunshot wounds.

Of those, eight remain in hospital, including the six-year-old, who is a Colombian national.

The other victims still hospitalised are two Colombians, a Canadian, a Russian, two US nationals and a Dutch woman.



What happened at the Columbine school shooting? The mass shooting at Columbine High School in Littleton, Colorado, took place on April 20, 1999. Twelve students and one teacher were murdered in the brutal massacre, carried out by Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold. The gunmen were two students who took their own lives before they could be captured. They burst onto campus wielding an arsenal of weapons, killing 13 and injuring at least 20 others. Dressed in trench coats, the demented duo began opening fire on pupils outside the school before moving inside and spraying bullets at victims in the library. It later emerged Harris and Klebold placed two duffel bags each containing a 20-pound propane bomb set to explode in the cafeteria. They then waited outside. But when the bombs failed to go off, they started gunning down students. A total of 188 rounds of ammunition were fired during the bloodbath. The students killed were between the ages of 14 and 17. At the time, Columbine was the worst high school shooting in US history. The horrifying attack inspired twisted copycats, including an 18-year-old who has killed herself after running around naked with a shotgun and making chilling threats to her school.

The Brazilian teen and four US citizens suffered injuries in the attack but were discharged from hospital.

Mexico’s Security Cabinet said in an initial statement: “According to preliminary information, a man fired shots at the site and later took his own life.”

It said authorities seized a firearm, a bladed weapon and live cartridges at the scene.



The oldest victim is a 61-year-old American tourist.

Witness Brenda Lee told CTV that one tourist jumped from the pyramid, desperate to escape the gunfire.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “Then a fellow jumped.

“It was someone trying to get away, and he dropped to the next level, but he fell on his back, and it was … it just was awful.”

News.title: Woman wakes up with mark on chest and people urge 'go to doctors'
News.content:
Woman wakes up with mark on chest and people urge 'go to doctors'

A woman woke up with strange, unidentified marks on her chest and had no idea what caused them but people have told her it could be an "emergency", urging her to go to the doctors

View Image The woman woke up with a strange mark on her chest (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

A woman woke up with two small marks on her chest and people have urged her to treat them as “an emergency”, and visit a doctor immediately to get checked out.

‌



Finding unexpected wounds or marks on your body can be an unnerving experience, with many people choosing to take photos of their scrapes, bruises and injuries and share them online in the hopes someone can identify a potential cause.

‌



This is exactly what one woman opted to do when she woke up with two round, red and raised marks on her chest. She posted an image of her injury on Reddit and simply said: “Woke up with these bite marks on my chest”.

‌



Fellow Reddit users were keen to weigh in with their theories and suggestions. It’s worth bearing in mind that any internet advice and comments based on photos a person has taken of their body will always be speculative.

If you have any concerns about your health, it’s best to book an appointment with a doctor for a detailed medical assessment and any necessary tests.

One Reddit user simply said: “Spider” while another agreed: “My vote is also spider; I have also gotten spider bites in my sleep; need not be a wolf spider.”

‌



A third referenced beloved comic book and film franchise superhero Spider-Man, who was famously bitten by a radioactive spider which imbued him with supernatural powers. They joked: “Do you wear glasses? You might not need them anymore”.

But others opted for a more serious response. One person said: “Public health inspector here. Please make sure it’s not a bat. If there’s even a possibility, you need rabies shots.”

The original poster replied: “I looked all over my house and couldn’t find any signs of a bat. My apartment is pretty small so I would think I would notice it in the morning at least when I woke up. Should I still get it?”

‌



She continued: “We didn’t have any windows open, and I don’t ever see or hear any bats in our area. I just saw a news story last year of a bat in our town that tested positive after biting someone”.

Someone else said: “That last part would probably take me to the doctor, just in case”.

‌



Another agreed: “OP [original poster], I’m an ER nurse. You can ask your doctor about it since your town has had rabid bats.”

And another said: “Go get a rabies shot. Your town has bats and a bat tested positive. This is an emergency, do not wait. You only have a limited time to get a rabies shot. Please go.”

But one person shared how this may not be so simple. They explained: “Idk [I don’t know] where OP lives but if this were me, I would be refused the shots if I went to the doctor or ER with OP’s story. I’d be labelled a hypochondriac and sent away, potentially asked to follow up with a therapist.”

Article continues below

The original poster replied: “This is exactly it. I’ve gotten rabies shots before for an encounter with a stray dog and it took so much convincing to get it. Not to mention expensive even with insurance. I don’t want to have to go through that again if it’s not absolutely necessary”.

Someone else added: “If you’ve gotten the rabies vaccine before you won’t get the immunoglobulin again which is the most expensive part. Just booster vaccines, current protocol is two booster doses of vaccine.”

The NHS states: “Rabies is a rare but serious infection that’s usually caught from a bite or scratch of an infected animal. It’s almost always fatal once symptoms appear, but vaccination and early treatment can prevent it.”

News.title: HMRC tax rule change from May 2026 is 'mandatory'
News.content:
HMRC tax rule change from May 2026 is 'mandatory'

A tax expert has warned of 'costly errors'

View 3 Images It was previously voluntary (Image: Yau Ming Low via Getty Images)

A tax expert is alerting people to a new HMRC rule that could catch people out. Conveyancing solicitors and payroll teams are among local professional advisers who may find themselves on the wrong side of the law from May – with penalties of up to £10,000 for compliance breaches. They must, under the wide definition of ‘tax adviser’, mandatorily register with HMRC by then if they interact or submit documents to the HMRC on behalf of clients.

‌



“There are going to be some costly errors made by unsuspecting organisations or individual sole traders who assist other people with their tax affairs,” warned Rick Schofield, a tax partner at Azets, an accountancy and business advisory firm. “This compliance shake-up is going to catch a lot of people out, the good as well as the bad, such as when it comes to stamp duty returns or chasing a PAYE code.”

‌



The scheme replaces a voluntary registration system.

‌



Rick, who specialises in advising on personal and company taxation matters, said: “The new regulations will affect all tax advisers who interact with HMRC on behalf of their clients – and tax advisers are those who provide professional tax advice and services, such as a conveyancing solicitor, but might not necessarily fall into the sole remit of accountants. Payroll teams are not exempt either – you must register even if it is an email or portal enquiry to chase a PAYE code for a member of staff.”

View 3 Images Rick Schofield, a tax partner at Azets (Image: Azets/Deep South Media)

Rick, who is based in Kent, said that advisers within professional partnerships were in the dark about whether the firm or the individual would be on the hook for breaches.

‌



He said: “Perhaps, to be on the safe side, partnerships may decide that it would be somewhat prudential for each partner to register with HMRC, even if they don’t submit the paperwork to HMRC in the normal course of their duties. It has been mooted by the accountancy profession, to Parliament, that the registration places unfair burdens on smaller tax adviser firms when compared to larger ones.

“Of course, everyone is looking to HMRC for an exhaustive dos and don’ts list, but nothing is forthcoming yet, adding to a sense of filing doom from May. People just want clarity and guidance.”

According to HMRC, the policy “ensures all tax advisers interacting with HMRC on behalf of their clients meet minimum standards”; that the changes “will improve HMRC’s ability to monitor and exclude tax advisers who are objectively unable to meet HMRC’s Standards for Agents or cannot lawfully act as a tax adviser”.

‌



A digital registration process will be available, with a non-digital alternative for those who are digitally excluded; HMRC states that it is investing £36m to modernise existing registration services. The process starts in May, with a transitional period of at least three months for all tax adviser groups; there are no registration fees.

View 3 Images HMRC is making changes (Image: Alamy/PA)

In a policy paper published last November, HMRC stated that individual taxpayers will not be directly affected by the requirement for their tax advisers, whether UK-based or overseas, to register with HMRC before they can act on their behalf.

Article continues below

Rick said: “However, individual taxpayers may be affected if their tax advisers are no longer able to act on their behalf because they are either unable to satisfy the new registration requirements imposed on (UK-based and overseas) tax advisers, or if their tax adviser is subject to sanction.

“You may see individual taxpayers left in expensive limbo, and facing late penalty fines, if their agents decline to send documentation to HMRC for whatever reason.”

Penalties range from £5,000 to £10,000. Payroll teams at companies are already under pressure with the government’s April 6 introduction of holiday pay compliance – the new Fair Work Agency can impose hefty fines or open criminal investigations for worker exploitation if paperwork is incorrect and staff are underpaid.

News.title: Iran could close second major trade route and still has huge stockpile of weapons
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Iran could close second major trade route and still has huge stockpile of weapons

Iranian chiefs issue strong hint of a secret weapon as it emerges they likely still have most of their deadly missiles and could now trigger a fresh blockade from Houthi proxies

View 6 Images Iran's proxy weapon the Yemeni Houthis (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Iranian forces likely still have 70% of their pre-conflict ballistic missiles, 60% of their launchers and at least 40% of their drone stockpiles, according to fresh intelligence analysis. News of Tehran’s deadly remaining arsenal emerged as Iran warned it still has “cards to play” in mockery of Donald Trump ’s language amid fears it could trigger the Yemeni Houthis.

‌



The rise in tension has heightened alarm in the region in the hours before the current two week ceasefire expires on Wednesday. If the Houthis become involved in the war there are increasing fears they could close the Baba el-Mandeb Strait, which has become a crucial alternative to the blockaded Hormuz passage.

‌



View 6 Images US President Donald Trump at White House (Image: Mehmet Eser/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

‌



Fears Iran war will explode again as defiant Tehran shuns peace talks despite Trump's threats READ MORE :

Iran war ramping up the risk of terrorism in UK - arson and drone attacks READ MORE :

Ali Abdollahi, commander of Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, which is its wartime command, said Tehran had the upper hand militarily. He added that he would not allow Donald Trump to “create false narratives over the situation on the ground,” as there were fresh warnings of a new Iranian war move.

Iranian parliamentary speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who is expected to head the Iranian delegation if peace talks take place in Pakistan, warned they were “prepared to reveal new cards on the battlefield.” He also said Iran would not accept negotiations with the US while under threat, adding today that “we have prepared to reveal new cards on the battlefield."

View 6 Images US VIce President JD Vance 'peace talks' (Image: Gage Skidmore/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

‌



A UK intelligence assessment report, seen by the Mirror, summarises the remaining Iran threat by writing: “US intelligence assessments have suggested that Iran likely still has access to around 70 percent of its pre-conflict ballistic missile stockpiles, and around 60 percent of its missile launchers.

“It also still retains around 40% of its drone arsenal. A senior official from Yemen’s Houthis has warned that the group could close the Bab al-Mandeb Strait if US President Donald Trump continues what he described as obstructing peace. The Bab al-Mandeb connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and is a key shipping route for global trade, particularly oil and other fuels moving between the Gulf, Europe and Asia.”

View 6 Images Fireball after Israeli strike on Tyre, southern Lebanon (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



If this happens it would mean a second closure of a major trade route as a result of the US-Iran war along with the Strait of Hormuz. It is thought US Vice President JD Vance will fly to Pakistan today hoping for peace talks with Iran.

He led the US team during failed talks with Iran earlier in the month, which collapsed after Iran would not agree to demands to end nuclear enrichment and hand over its 440kg of highly enriched uranium. The Iranians have said they do not trust US, and wanted assurances they would not be attacked again if a final agreement was reached.

View 6 Images Gathering belongings at site of air-strike (Image: AP)

‌



Pakistan has locked down security, suspending public transport in the capital. Islamabad’s electricity board also promised that power cuts would be suspended in the city while negotiations continue. Iran has not yet confirmed it will turn up for the talks.

Distrust between the two sides has grown as a result of Iran coming under attack several times before whilst peace negotiations were underway. The regime fears more talks could be a cover for a fresh attack.

View 6 Images RAF Lakenheath and US fighter takes off (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Iran’s High Council for Human Rights has condemned US attacks on religious, cultural and historical sites across the country, saying the attacks reveal a deliberate attempt to destroy symbols of religious minorities. The claims were made through state media.

That includes a claimed strike on the Tehran Jewish Synagogue, a historic place of worship, as well as damage to the Nicholas Orthodox Cathedral and St Mary Greek Orthodox Church. The statement said: "These attacks not only demonstrate the complete disregard of these aggressor regimes for basic human rights and international standards, but are evidence of a sinister intention to eliminate the identity symbols of religious minorities in Iran."

News.title: 'Feel cosy and calm' with £7 Home Bargains item that's 'perfect for bedrooms'
News.content:
'Feel cosy and calm' with £7 Home Bargains item that's 'perfect for bedrooms'

These affordable curtains make rooms 'feel more peaceful and comfortable'

View 3 Images The large curtains cost less than £10 (Image: Google)

Home Bargains shoppers can 'feel calm and cosy' with a £7 item that offers a feature "perfect for bedrooms". The store is popular across the UK for selling almost anything under one roof at affordable prices.

Shoppers can update their windows with large blackout curtains available in three colours from the Home Collections range. The store's Home Collections Blackout Single Curtain lets homeowners block incoming light and create rooms that feel "more peaceful and comfortable" without bright sunlight seeping in.

In the product description, the discount brand said: "Bring a warm, comfy vibe into your space with the Home Collections Blackout Curtain set. Each pack comes with one panel, giving you plenty of coverage for larger windows.

"The curtains are designed with four sturdy rings that easily slide onto most standard-diameter rods, so hanging them up is quick and hassle-free. The blackout fabric helps keep out bright sunlight, reduces glare, and adds a little extra privacy - perfect for bedrooms, living rooms, or anywhere you want a cosy, calm atmosphere."

Home Bargains' bosses also claim that the material is "soft to the touch". It can offer an affordable way to add "simple style" to a home that "feels more peaceful and comfortable".

Shoppers should be aware that these curtains are available only in one size. The website lists the curtains as 137cm wide with a 218cm drop. Similar curtains cost much more elsewhere, such as these £25 Berlin Blackout Eyelet Curtains from Dunelm (measuring 117cm wide by 228cm drop).

View 3 Images The Home Collections Blackout Single Curtain (Image: Home Bargains)

These curtains should be available in any of the 600+ Home Bargains stores across the UK, but shoppers can also place an online order with the retailer for delivery. Shoppers can avoid paying a £3.95 delivery fee (for UK mainland) if their order exceeds £100 when buying eligible items.

On the Home Bargains website, shoppers can find more homeware at affordable prices. See the full selection here.

There are many items that can help upgrade homes on a budget, from pretty decorations to practical furniture pieces. One such item is an IKEA-style cabinet that solves a common hallway problem.

View 3 Images Shoppers can pick from black, silver and charcoal (Image: Home Bargains)

Describing the cabinet online, Home Bargains bosses said: "Keep your hallway neat, tidy, and totally clutter-free with this sleek Two-Tier Shoe Cabinet. Designed with a slim profile that fits perfectly in small spaces, it offers a stylish way to store footwear while keeping everything hidden and organised.

Article continues below

"With room to hold up to eight pairs of shoes, it’s ideal for busy households, sneaker lovers, or anyone who’s tired of tripping over stray footwear. The smooth pull-down compartments make it easy to grab what you need on the go, while the top surface is perfect for plants, candles, or décor that adds personality to your entryway."

Gardens can also be given an upgrade in time for warmer weather with new Home Bargains items. Recently, the store updated its 'grass' animal collection with an option that makes outdoor spaces appear more " playful and charming".

News.title: Man launched 'MMA sex attack' on Brit tourist in Tenerife and 'battered Brit pensioners'
News.content:
Man launched 'MMA sex attack' on Brit tourist in Tenerife and 'battered Brit pensioners'

Police have arrested a man who is alleged to have sexually assaulted a female British tourist and robbed an elderly couple from the UK on the same day in Tenerife

View 2 Images A man has been arrested in Tenerife (Image: Getty Images)

Police have arrested a man who is alleged to have sexually assaulted a female British tourist and violently robbed an elderly couple from the UK on the same day.

‌



The suspect assaulted the woman in the south of Tenerife after using a martial arts technique known as "lion-killer chokehold", which left her semi-conscious, a spokesman for Spain's National Police said. The young woman had lost her mobile phone and the suspect had offered to help her. "Taking advantage of the fact they were in a secluded and lonely place, the individual attacked her by surprise," the spokesman added.

‌



On the same day as the alleged sex attack, the man allegedly targeted an 89-year-old British man and his 79-year-old wife. Both tourists were hospitalised after the suspect assaulted them "with his fists and his feet" when the woman threw her husband’s watch into the bushes after it came off during a struggle, the spokesman said.

‌



View 2 Images Spanish police have arrested a suspect in relation to reports of a sexual assault and two violent robberies in the south of Tenerife (file) (Image: Getty Images)

The suspect has also been linked to another incident on March 20, in which a Swedish tourist was "violently" grabbed "by the neck", with her necklace ripped off, the spokesman said.

‌



The spokesman for Spain's National Police said: "Officers have arrested the suspected author of a crime of sexual assault and two robberies with violence committed in the south of Tenerife."

The first incident took place towards the end of March in the Las Veronicas area. The victim alerted police and provided images taken the same night in which the suspect appeared, which police said proved key towards progressing the investigation.

Officers were separately investigating two reports of violent robberies in the same municipality of Arona, one of which took place on the same day as the alleged sexual assault and another three days earlier.

Article continues below

The spokesman continued: "In both cases, the areas where the incidents occurred, as well as the physical description of the suspect and the extreme violence employed all matched. In one of the robberies the victims were an elderly couple. The mugger tried to steal the man's watch, and a tussle occurred between both, which ended with the watch on the floor.

"At this moment the man's wife picked it up and threw it into an area of bushes to avoid it being taken. This provoked a violent reaction by the attacker who assaulted both victims with his fists and his feet, managing finally to take a bag full of their shopping that they were carrying. A female witness managed to take a photograph of the mugger, which was provided to police investigators.

Sources said on Tuesday that the suspect had incredibly been released on bail after going before a duty judge as opposed to being remanded to prison pending charges and trial.

'Look younger' with reduced £75 serum now £15 at Home Bargains in online deal

Shoppers can take advantage of the 80% off discount online

View 3 Images Home Bargains says it is designed to create a 'youthful glow' (stock image) (Image: Getty)

Home Bargains shoppers can enjoy an 80% discount on a serum designed to "help skin look renewed for a visibly smoother, more youthful appearance". The budget store often reduces the price of high-end items to a fraction of their original cost, and a recently added StarBuy offer is no exception.

Home Bargains is selling Kiehls Retinol Fast Release Wrinkle-Reducing Night Serum for far less than its recommended retail price. The 28ml bottle comes with a 1g powder capsule to mix in, and together they usually cost £75, but Home Bargains customers only need to spend £14.99.

‌



The deal is online-only, meaning shoppers won't find it in stores, and they'll have to head online if interested. Home Bargains says the retinol serum "works deep within the skin’s surface" and claims it "helps speed up skin renewal in five days."

‌



It also claims that the serum "helps reduce the appearance of fine lines in five days". According to the product description, the fresh-mix packaging also helps keep the retinol "potent until first use".

The full description reads: "Kiehls Retinol Fast Release Night Serum from the Simple family boosts skin renewal with potent retinol, visibly reducing fine lines in just five days for a smoother, youthful glow. Its fresh-mix packaging keeps the formula super effective."

View 3 Images Kiehls Retinol Fast Release Wrinkle-Reducing Night Serum 28ml (Image: Home Bargains )

It continues: "This fast-acting 0.3% Retinol night serum accelerates skin surface cell renewal with Retinol that penetrates up to 15 surface layers deep into the skin. Experience visible reduction of fine lines in just five days and visible improvement in deep wrinkles in two weeks.

"To ensure maximum efficacy its innovative packaging isolates a high concentration of pure Retinol powder so it can be freshly mixed into the serum upon first use. With continuous use this night serum with Retinol helps skin look renewed for a visibly smoother more youthful appearance."

According to Boots, retinol increases the rate of skin cell turnover and promotes collagen production. "Because of this, retinol helps exfoliate the skin and unclog pores whilst improving the look of fine lines, wrinkles, uneven skin tone and pigmentation," the store says.

‌



View 3 Images The £14.99 skincare deal is an online-only offer

Elsewhere at Home Bargains, it has added new haircare deals to its range of beauty products that claim to "strengthen hair against breakage", and leave it feeling "20 times stronger". Bottles are normally sold for almost £50 but have been cut down to less than £10 in a recent sale.

The Sebastian Professional No. Breaker Rebalancing Bonding Pre-Shampoo is the latest item to be added to the Home Bargains' range of SpecialBuy products. But, shoppers will not be able to pick up this offer in any of the 600+ stores across the UK.

News.title: Donald Trump issues confusing fresh Iran war update over nuclear weapons
News.content:
Donald Trump issues confusing fresh Iran war update over nuclear weapons

Donald Trump previously claimed Iran was weeks away from making a weapon of mass destruction despite last year claiming nuclear sites in the country had been obliterated

View 3 Images Donald Trump issued a bizarre Iran war update (Image: ALLISON ROBBERT/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock)

Donald Trump has issued a bizarre and confusing Iran war update claiming the country's nuclear sites had already been obliterated.

‌



The US President shared the claim that appeared to contradict his stated war aim of stopping Iran from making a nuclear weapon. Trump lashed out at "fake news" in the post and once again repeated last year's strikes on Iran had destroyed Iran's nuclear sites.

‌



"Operation Midnight Hammer was a complete and total obliteration of the Nuclear Dust sites in Iran," Trump said in a TruthSocial post. "Therefore, digging it out will be a long and difficult process. Fake News CNN, and other corrupt Media Networks and Platforms, fail to give our great aviators the credit they deserve - Always trying to demean and belittle - LOSERS!!!"

‌



View 3 Images Trump's decision to go to war is unpopular in the US (Image: AP)

While Trump appeared to reference difficulty in obtaining materials needed to create a bomb, it also undermined one of his stated objectives for the war. In March, Trump said Iran had been about "two to four weeks" away from obtaining a nuclear weapon as justification for the current war in the Middle East.

Operation Midnight Hammer saw the destruction of nuclear sites in Iran as part of the joint US-Israel Twelve-Day War in June of last year. Trump and his administration declared the operation a success, claiming it had "obliterated" Iran's nuclear programme.

‌



Analysts at the time were sceptical the attack had completely destroyed Iran's nuclear capabilities, although the majority agreed the regime faced a serious set back in its uranium enrichment production. The claim Iran's nuclear sites had been "obliterated" stands in contrast to the inconsistent explanations given by the Trump administration for the start of the war.

View 3 Images Trump has given multiple justifications for the war (Image: AP)

Among reasons given for the current war include to stop Iranian missile capabilities, preventing Iran from building a nuclear weapon, regime change and seizing the country's oil resources. A ceasefire between Iran and the US came into effect a couple of weeks ago and no permanent end to the conflict has been negotiated in the days since.

Article continues below

Trump has repeatedly claimed the war would be coming to an end within weeks, only for it to continue. Negotiations to bring about an end to the conflict ended with the US walking away after a single day of talks in Pakistan.

Pakistan is due to host a second round of peace talks, though there is no indication a swift end to the war is in sight. The conflict has since affected the global economy, sending oil prices spiking across the world.

The vital Strait of Hormuz is a major oil shipping lane and has faced closure and blockades from Iran and the US, respectively. In a bizarre twist, Pakistan could be pulled into the conflict against Iran having signed a defence pact with Saudi Arabia, which has faced attacks from Tehran's proxies.

News.title: UK homes 'can claim £9,000' after new rule change announced today
News.content:
UK homes 'can claim £9,000' after new rule change announced today

The Government is increasing the threshold

View 3 Images The scheme is being changed (Image: brebca via Getty Images)

Households will be able to claim up to £9,000 after the Government announced it was raising the amount available through a scheme. Those struggling with the soaring costs of heating oil will receive larger grants to swap their oil boilers for electric heat pumps, the Government has confirmed.

‌



Ministers are boosting grants under the "boiler upgrade scheme", which currently provides £7,500 for households to replace their fossil fuel boiler with a heat pump, to £9,000 for properties dependent on heating oil and LPG.

‌



Officials say the move will benefit households and small businesses in England and Wales, particularly those in rural locations, helping them to electrify their heating and gain greater stability over their energy bills. Families heating their homes with heating oil or LPG have faced rocketing costs in the aftermath of the Iran war.

‌



Data reveals that prices for heating oil – which is not covered by the Ofgem energy price cap that shields consumers with gas boilers from extreme energy price spikes – doubled to record highs between February and March.

View 3 Images There are new worries over energy bills (Image: John Lamb via Getty Images)

The Government has already pledged £53 million in targeted support for "vulnerable" heating oil consumers, focusing on "those households that are most exposed".

‌



Simon Francis, co-ordinator of the End Fuel Poverty Coalition, said: "Heating oil and LPG customers have been among the hardest hit by the current crisis.

"The three million households relying on these fuels sit outside the energy price cap and have no equivalent protection when global prices spike.

"These households are disproportionately in rural areas, have lower incomes, and live in older, harder-to-upgrade properties."

‌



He noted that while the £9,000 grant for such homes would be "very welcome", it might not fully cover the costs for those unable to afford the remainder or whose properties require substantial preparatory work before a heat pump can be fitted.

View 3 Images A heat pump (Image: Alamy/PA)

According to the Energy Saving Trust, installing an air source heat pump typically costs around £11,000, though this varies depending on the pump's size, the property's dimensions and age, and any necessary upgrades like new radiators.

Article continues below

Mr Francis explained: "Therefore, the expansion of this scheme must be accompanied by specialist local advice for households, stronger consumer protections during the works, and targeted additional support for those who cannot meet the shortfall.

"The measure of success is not how many grants are issued, but whether the households most exposed to fossil fuel price shocks are genuinely better off as a result."

South Korea police said on Tuesday they are seeking to arrest music mogul Bang Si-Hyuk, chairman of the agency behind K-pop supergroup BTS, as they expand an investigation into allegations that he illegally gained more than $100m in an investor fraud scheme.

The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency confirmed that it has asked prosecutors to request a court warrant for Mr Bang’s arrest.

Mr Bang has been under investigation since November over allegations that he misled investors in 2019 by telling them HYBE had no plans to go public, inducing them to sell their shares to a private equity fund before the company proceeded with an initial public offering. Police believe that the fund may have paid Bang around 200 billion won ($136m) in a side deal that promised him 30 per cent of post-IPO stock sale profits.

( Getty )

Mr Bang, a music executive and producer who founded HYBE as Big Hit Entertainment in 2005, is widely seen as one of the most powerful figures in K-pop, overseeing some of the industry’s most popular acts, including Seventeen, Le Sserafim and Katseye in addition to BTS.

Mr Bang’s legal troubles are a major public relations setback for HYBE, coming as BTS embarks on a global tour after a nearly four-year hiatus as its members served for mandatory military service.

BTS performed in front of tens of thousands of international fans at a free comeback concert in Seoul last month and have also held several concerts in South Korea’s Goyang city and Tokyo. The group is to kick off a series of US events with a concert in Tampa, Florida, later this month.

Representatives of Bang’s agency, HYBE, did not immediately respond to AP’s requests for comment.

Shaun Murphy has criticised fellow former world champions Ronnie O’Sullivan and Judd Trump for missing the launch of the 2026 World Championship in Sheffield.

This year’s players gathered in Tudor Square outside the Crucible Theatre on Friday for a green-carpet ceremony celebrating the relationship between snooker and Sheffield, before media commitments with press and broadcasters inside the venue.

But O’Sullivan and Trump did not appear and unless they can provide a valid reason for their absence, such as a medical issue, they face a sanction from the World Snooker Tour.

Murphy said: “I think it’s become normal that they don’t turn up for these types of things. I think it’s a real shame, and they probably could both have done a little bit more to help promote the game over the years.

“I think it might give those two an image problem when the public tag onto that and realise that two of the biggest stars of the game weren’t here for the opening day. It’s a strange one.”

Shaun Murphy has criticised Ronnie O'Sullivan and Judd Trump for failing to do more to promote their sport ( PA )

Trump won the world title in 2019 and will be one of the favourites the lift the trophy when the tournament gets going on Saturday. He begins his tournament against former semi-finallist Gary Wilson, who came through qualifying to reach this year’s event.

O’Sullivan is meanwhile chasing history as he seeks a record eighth world title, and the 50-year-old has recently recaptured some of his best form to be in with a chance of winning the Crucible showpiece for the first time since 2022.

O’Sullivan recently indicated his intention to travel into the tournament from a base in Ireland. He has rejected all media requests in the build-up and will not be involved in his regular punditry role with TNT Sports.

He begins his campaign against Chinese debutant He Guoqiang, who holds a winning record against the player widely regarded as the best of all time, having triumphed twice in their three past meetings.

If O’Sullivan gets through that match, then his second-round contest will be against either fellow class of ‘92 great John Higgins or long-time adversary Ali Carter.

O’Sullivan’s no-show follows his brief walk-out during the first frame of his World Open match against Ross Muir last month because a sponsorship logo on his waistcoat appeared to be distracting him.

The “Rocket” was put off by the red advert stitched to the right side of his chest when lining up a black, midway through a break during his first-round match. He briefly scratched at the patch in an attempt to remove it before exiting the auditorium, causing a delay of several minutes.

Muir was left confused in his seat until O’Sullivan returned, following some alterations, to claim the first frame on his way to a 5-1 win in Yushan, China.

Zhao Xintong will begin the tournament against qualifier Liam Highfield on Saturday morning as he looks to beat the so-called "Crucible curse" and become the first first-time champion at the venue to successfully defend his crown.

An individual's genetic makeup could influence the effectiveness of weight-loss injections, a new study suggests.

Researchers discovered that specific gene variants can predict both the degree of weight loss achieved and an individual's likelihood of experiencing side effects like nausea and vomiting.

This insight could partially explain why some people lose weight faster than others on these medications, while others are more vulnerable to adverse reactions.

Published in the journal Nature, the findings offer a pathway towards developing precision medicine, allowing doctors to tailor treatments based on genetic profiles.

The new study examined data from almost 28,000 people registered to the genetics website 23andMe and self-reported data on their use of GLP-1 receptor agonist weight-loss treatments including semaglutide, such as Wegovy, and tirzepatide, also known as Mounjaro.

Using genetic data, researchers found that variations in two genes involved with hormones in the gut, which regulate appetite and digestion, could play a role in how these drugs work.

One, the GLP1 receptor variant rs10305420, was associated with a slightly greater decrease in body mass index (BMI) among people taking GLP-1 drugs.

Researchers found that variations in two genes involved with hormones in the gut, which regulate appetite and digestion, could play a role in how these drugs work ( James Manning/PA )

Another, rs1800437 in the gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor gene, was linked with side effects of nausea and vomiting in people taking tirzepatide, but was not associated with how much weight they lost.

The researchers, led by experts from 23andMe and The University of Copenhagen, said that these genetic differences may partially account for differences in weight loss.

Though other non-genetic factors play a role, including gender, age and which treatment a person takes.

“Our study detected a robust genetic association with GLP-1 medication weight loss efficacy and associated side effects,” the authors wrote.

But they stressed that the effect was “modest” as they called for future studies to explore the role of genetics in these treatments further.

Commenting on the paper, Dr Marie Spreckley, research programme manager at the University of Cambridge, said the study “provides biologically plausible evidence that variation in the drug target itself (GLP1R) and related pathways (GIPR) contributes to inter-individual variability in response.

“However, the magnitude of these genetic effects is small in clinical terms.

“Importantly, non-genetic factors such as sex, drug type, dose, and duration appear to explain a substantially larger proportion of variability.”

Dr Spreckley added: “In terms of how this fits with the wider evidence, it reinforces that while there is substantial variability in response to GLP-1 therapies, genetics is only one part of a much more complex picture.

“Behavioural, clinical, and treatment-related factors remain the dominant drivers of outcomes.

“Overall, this is an important step towards understanding variability and the potential for future precision approaches, but the effects are modest and the evidence is not yet sufficient to support using genetic information to guide treatment decisions in routine clinical practice.”

A batch of blood pressure medication is being recalled after a potential manufacturing error meant some packets may contain the wrong dose.

The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) warned batches of Ramipril 10mg capsules, manufactured by Crescent Pharma Limited, may contain blister strips of a lower dose, specifically Ramipril 5mg, due to a potential manufacturing error.

It comes after a patient found one blister pack of Ramipril 5mg capsules inside a sealed carton of Ramipril 10mg capsules.

Both product batches were manufactured at the same site, and the error appears to have occurred during secondary packaging of the cartons.

The regulator has advised pharmacy and healthcare professionals to stop supplying the impacted batch of medication and return all remaining stock to their suppliers.

open image in gallery Batches of a blood pressure medication are being recalled as some packs contain the wrong dose ( PA )

However, the risk to patients taking the lower dose of this medicine for a short time is very low, the MHRA said.

Ramipril is taken by millions of people worldwide to treat high blood pressure and heart failure. It’s also prescribed after a heart attack.

The medication helps to prevent strokes, heart attacks and kidney problems by widening the blood vessels which makes it easier for the heart to pump blood around the body.

Dr Alison Cave, MHRA chief safety officer, said: “If you take Ramipril 10mg, check the packaging for batch number GR174091. The batch number and expiry date information can be found on the outer carton.

“If you have received this batch, check that the medication name on the carton matches the blister strips inside.

“If the 10 mg carton of Ramipril contains blister strips that are labelled as Ramipril 5mg capsules, contact your dispensing pharmacy.

“If the carton contains blister strips that are correctly labelled as Ramipril 10mg capsules, you do not need to take further action.”

open image in gallery MHRA warned batches of Ramipril 10mg capsules, manufactured by Crescent Pharma Limited, may contain blister strips of a lower dose, specifically Ramipril 5mg ( Getty/iStock )

Those who are experiencing adverse effects after taking the lower doses that were packaged in error are being urged to seek medical advice.

But the MHRA reassured that there is a very low risk to health from taking a lower dose than prescribed.

Both strengths of the medication are used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure, and kidney disease.

Any possible impact of a lower dose of Ramipril is expected to be gradual rather than immediate or life threatening.

Depending on why a patient has been prescribed ramipril, the usual starting dose is between 1.25mg and 2.5mg once a day, to ensure it does not make the patient feel dizzy.

The dose is usually increased gradually over a few weeks with the maximum dose being 5mg twice a day or 10mg once a day.

George RR Martin’s Elden Ring is the latest video game to be adapted for the big screen – with Heartstopper star Kit Connor leading the impressive cast.

The fantasy role-playing game, which was co-written by the Game of Thrones author, came out in 2022 to universal acclaim, picking up multiple Bafta Game Awards and selling over 30 million copies worldwide.

It follows one of the Tarnished – an exiled member of fictional setting the Lands Between – as they attempt to repair the Elden Ring after it was shattered by ruler Queen Marika.

The game is set to become a live-action film, written and directed by Ex_Machina and Civil War’s Alex Garland.

open image in gallery Kit Connor is starring in the upcoming 'Elden Ring' adaptation ( Getty )

Set for release in March 2028, production company A24 has now revealed its star-studded cast, with Connor being joined by Paddington’s Ben Whishaw, Beef star Cailee Spaeny, Strike’s Tom Burke and Bottoms actor Havana Rose Liu.

Others in the cast include Oscar-nominated actor Jonathan Pryce, Sonoya Mizuno, who starred in Ex_Machina, Margo’s Got Money Troubles’ Nick Offerman, Dear England’s John Hodgkinson, House of the Dragon’s Jefferson Hall, A Haunting in Venice’s Emma Laird and comedian Peter Serafinowicz.

The plot behind the film and the cast’s characters are yet to be revealed.

Sharing the news on Instagram, Connor – who previously worked with Garland on Modern Warfare – said that he is “ridiculously proud to be a part of this team”.

While Laird, who currently stars in BBC One crime drama, added: “So excited about this one!! Shoutout to all my gamer friends and my brother for the Elden Ring education.”

The news received a warm reception from fans, with one writing on X: “That cast feels less like blockbuster cosplay and more like they actually want the world to feel eerie and ruined. The real test is still whether they keep the mystery intact.”

open image in gallery 'Beef' star Cailee Spaeny also makes up the cast ( Getty )

Another said: “The live-action ELDEN RING cast is STACKED. Alex Garland directing?? yeah this might actually be insane.”

It’s been a successful few years for video game adaptations, with the Super Mario Bros Movie smashing box office records in 2023 despite poor reviews from critics.

Despite The Independent’s Clarisse Loughrey calling it an adventure in “comfortable mediocrity” at the time, it took home over $1.360bn (£1.006bn) around the world after opening in April that year.

Last year, A Minecraft Movie achieved a similar feat, becoming the highest-grossing video game adaptation in its opening weekend. It ultimately took home $967m (£716m) at the box office.

News.title: Wage growth slumps to five-year low
News.content:
Workers are seeing the slowest pay rises in more than five years in a blow to households already facing soaring bills triggered by the war in Iran.

Average wages grew by 3.6pc in the three months to February, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). This was the weakest rise since the quarter to November 2020.

Adjusting for inflation, British workers’ pay increased by only 0.2pc.

Slowing wages will raise the pressure on families, as the war in Iran pushes up the cost of living.

The ongoing conflict is expected to drive up food inflation to more than 9pc by the end of the year, according to forecasts by the Food and Drink Federation. Average households energy bills are expected to rise close to £2,000 a year, while petrol and diesel prices have already spiked.

Martin Beck, chief economist at WPI Strategy, said: “Weaker pay growth will compound the squeeze on households from higher energy prices and supply chain disruption linked to the conflict in the Middle East.

“While recent diplomatic developments may limit the worst-case outcomes, a period of falling real wages is still likely in the second half of the year, weighing on consumer spending and, in turn, labour demand.”

The public sector is better protected, with wages still growing by 5.2pc annually compared with a rise of 3.2pc in the private sector.

Unemployment surprisingly fell before the conflict, the ONS said, though it remains the hardest time since Covid to find a job with far more jobseekers than open roles.

The jobless rate fell to 4.9pc in December to February, down from 5.1pc in the previous three months.

Economists said the fall was mainly driven by rising economic inactivity, meaning they are no longer classified as unemployed, rather than more people finding work.

Modupe Adegbembo at Jefferies said: “This apparent improvement was entirely flattered by falling participation rather than stronger hiring. The decline in labour force participation mechanically reduced the unemployment rate, masking continued softness in actual labour demand.”

The number of employees on the nation’s payroll fell by 65,000 in the year to March.

Job losses have been concentrated among younger workers, with 242,000 fewer people under the age of 35 in work since since Rachel Reeves’s maiden Budget in October 2024, ONS figures show. By contrast, there are almost 100,000 more people aged 35 and older employed compared to October 2024.

There are now 2.5 unemployed people per vacancy, which makes it is the toughest time to find work since early 2021.

The number of advertised jobs fell to 711,000 in March, the lowest number in five years. Outside of the pandemic, vacancies are at an 11-year low.

Signs of weakness in the jobs market mean the Bank of England is less likely to increase interest rates, Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said.

Mr Pugh added that we could still see large rises in unemployment this year, despite the recent fall.

He said: “We now think the unemployment rate will probably peak at around 5.5pc. If energy prices rise higher over the summer as supply becomes even more constricted, the unemployment rate could move towards 6pc.”

News.title: One-in-three Russians should be tested for HIV every year, urges health minister
News.content:
A third of Russia’s population should be tested for HIV every year, its health minister has urged, in a sign an epidemic downplayed by the Kremlin is spiralling.

Mikhail Murashko said screening was essential to curb the transmission of the virus, which has exploded among Russian troops and the broader population since Moscow launched its invasion of Ukraine.

“Further expansion of medical testing is necessary. Every third citizen should be tested, with particular attention to at-risk groups,” the Russian Health Ministry quoted him as saying last week.

Since 2022, Russia has been in the top five countries for new HIV cases, according to the UN. Only South Africa, Mozambique, Nigeria and India had more.

When the figures were released, the Russian health ministry dismissed them as “provocative propaganda” and accused the UN of attempting to “falsify statistical data”.

While Russia has long had high rates of HIV, it now has the highest prevalence in Europe, with 890 cases per 100,000 people, according to World Health Organization (WHO) data. The rate is comparable to that of Liberia, Sierra Leone or Guinea.

An estimated 1.1 million Russians, or nearly one per cent of the population, are now living with the virus.

Experts warn the true figure may be much higher, given how many cases go undetected and unreported.

“Infection risks are very high,” said Vadim Pokrovsky, the head of Russia’s Federal Scientific and Methodological Centre for Aids Prevention and Control. “If we look only at adults aged 15 to 50, more than one per cent are infected – that is, every hundredth person.”

Among men in their early forties, the rate climbs to around one in 25, he added.

News.title: Severe malaria may do long-lasting damage to children’s brains, major study finds
News.content:
Severe malaria may be doing long-lasting damage to children’s brains, according to a major study in Uganda.

Researchers collected data on a group of nearly 1,000 children up to 15 years after infection and found that those who had survived cerebral malaria or severe anaemia caused by malaria performed worse on cognitive tests many years later.

Cerebral malaria is considered the most severe form of the disease and occurs when infected blood cells get stuck inside small blood vessels in the brain, restricting blood flow and causing swelling, often leading to a coma and death.

Along with anaemia, it is believed to affect up to two million children each year, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa, causing hundreds of thousands of deaths.

The research, which was published in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) last week, is the latest in a series of studies on the impact of severe malaria led by Paul Bangira of the Makerere University Hospital in Kampala, Uganda, and Chandy John of Indiana University.

Known as the Malarial Impact on Neurobehavioral Development (MIND) study, the researchers have been following the same cohort of 1,438 children since 2008.

The first study found that children who had cerebral malaria scored lower on cognitive tests two years after their infection while a second, carried out between 2014 and 2018, confirmed these results.

The most recent test began in 2020, with the researchers hoping to find out whether the children’s cognitive deficits had improved. They managed to track down 939 of the original cohort and had them sit tests in mathematics, reading, attention and overall cognition.

News.title: Household confidence plunges to three-year low on Iran war
News.content:
Household concerns about personal finances have hit a three-year high as the Iran war threatens a fresh spike in inflation.

Consumers’ confidence over their financial wellbeing fell its lowest level since July 2023, according to a survey of 1,500 UK households.

The S&P Global UK Consumer Sentiment Index showed households were more pessimistic about the year ahead as the conflict in the Middle East creates “growing unease”.

Maryam Baluch, economist at S&P Global, said people were expecting higher interest rates from the Bank of England to combat an expected surge in inflation.

The war has driven up the price of petrol by 25p a litre, with diesel almost 50p per litre above pre-war levels.

Money markets indicate the Bank of England will raise interest rates at least once this year as a result of the conflict. Traders had expected rate cuts before the war broke out.

Ms Baluch said: “Increased energy-market disruption raises the odds of further spikes in fuel and utility bills, with headwinds keeping near-term inflation stickier than policymakers would like.”

She added: “The strain on finances and an uncertain central bank policy outlook is showing up in consumer behaviour as households bear down on spending, particularly on big-ticket items, while running down savings at the fastest pace in a year.

“Debt undertakings, too, edged higher with the need for loans growing to the greatest extent in over two-and-a-half years.”
